previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her eighth cycle of high-dose methotrexate for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. She tolerated the chemotherapy well, with no signs of mucositis or infection. Methotrexate was administered at a reduced dose of 3500 mg/m² and followed by leucovorin rescue. Her methotrexate level declined to 0.03, allowing discharge. She remained neutropenic with an ANC of 420 but was afebrile and stable. Diabetes management included holding metformin during admission and increasing the dose upon discharge. Potassium supplementation was initiated due to hypokalemia. Prophylactic ciprofloxacin was prescribed for neutropenia. The patient was discharged home with instructions to continue leucovorin, monitor for infection, and follow up for lab testing and oncology evaluation.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ yo F with type 2 diabetes, common variable 
immune deficiency on chronic IVIG since ___, asthma, chronic 
back pain, and primary colonic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma 
(s/p 4 cycles of R-EPOCH) with CNS involvement, presenting for

# Jejunal inflammation: patient reported few day history of GI 
upset prior to admission which she related to food indiscretion 
at a barbecue. She had been afebrile but slightly tender on 
exam. Given history of colonic lymphoma, a CT abdomen was done 
prior to proceeding with scheduled HD-MTX to rule out recurrence 
of GI lymphoma. Patient was started on cipro and flagyl for 
empiric GI pathogen coverage. CT abd showed bowel wall 
thickening in the jejunum which was likely consistent with 
infection though a more distal area of submucosal edema could be 
concerning for lymphoma. GI was consulted and proceeded with 
small bowel enteroscopy, which did not show any abnormalities in 
the small bowel (only mild gastritis). However, distal area 
concerning for lymphoma on CT was not reached with enteroscope. 
Biopsy was not done because there were no abnormal findings. 
Patient improved clinically completely to baseline and had no 
more abdominal pain, abnormal ostomy output or other symptoms. 
Stool culture was negative for C diff and other pathogens. Given 
clinical improvement, patient was discharged on 7-day course of 
cipro/flagyl but will follow up with Dr. ___ Dr. ___ 
(___) next week. PPI was increased to twice daily given gastritis 
seen on EGD. She has a PET scan scheduled in a few days and if 
that has any abnormalities or if she experiences recurrence of 
symptoms, an MR enteroscopy can be considered to better evaluate 
the GI tract. She did not receive any chemotherapy on this 
admission.
.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,
  
You were initially admitted for your scheduled cycle of 
methotrexate. You had reported few days of GI discomfort and 
given your history of colon lymphoma we did imaging studies to 
evaluate for recurrence. A CT of your abdomen showed some bowel 
wall thickening which can be found in infection (like viral 
gastroenteritis) or lymphomas. You had an enteroscopy to look 
inside your small bowel and this was normal, though it did not 
extend to the area with concerning inflammation. Your symptoms 
improved and you did not have any more abdominal discomfort, and 
able to eat and drink well. Because of this, it is most likely 
that you had an infectious process in your bowel that has now 
resolved. However, we would like you to follow up next week with 
Dr. ___ in GI and Dr. ___, and to go to your PET scan on 
___. Depending on how you feel at that time and what the PET 
scan shows, we may decide to do further imaging of your abdomen 
with an MRI.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History of lymphoma, with new onset abdominal pain.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained from the thoracic inlet
to the pubic symphysis after administration of IV and oral contrast.

COMPARISON:  CT ___ and ___.

CT CHEST:  Thyroid gland is normal in appearance with symmetric enhancement.
Scattered non-enlarged lymph nodes are seen at the axilla.  There is a single
subcarinal lymph node which is essentially unchanged from the prior study
measuring 1.4 cm.  No interval changes seen scarring  within the bilateral
upper lobes.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  There is no
pericardial effusion.  Right sided port-a-cath terminates in the superior vena
cava.

CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:  The liver is normal in appearance without focal
lesion, intra- or extra-hepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  The gallbladder is
normal without evidence of gallstones.  The pancreas, kidneys, and adrenal
glands are unremarkable.  The spleen is enlarged measuring 15.5 cm as before.
The patient is status post small bowel resection with end colostomy.
Otherwise, the distal esophagus, stomach and intra-abdominal large and small
bowel are normal in appearance.  Enlarged enhancing retroperitoneal lymph node
is again seen essentially unchanged in size measuring 1.3 x0.7 cm (2:74).
There are scattered nonenlarged retroaortic and periaortic and mesenteric
lymph nodes again seen.  

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:  The patient is status post ___ pouch and end
colostomy which is unchanged in appearance.  The bladder and uterus are
normal.  There are no pathologically enlarged lymph nodes in the pelvis or
inguinal areas.Small free fluid is seen in the pelvis.

GASTROINTESTINAL:  The stomach and duodenum are normal.  Changes of small
bowel resection are noted, with suture lines in the mid abdomen and mid pelvis
are seen. Just distal to the jejunal anastomosis site, there is diffuse
moderate submucosal bowel wall edema and enhancement extending over
approximately 11cm in length. This may represent inflammation versus
lymphomatous involvement.  Also seen is mild pneumatosis within the distal
segment of this abnormal loop which shows more diffuse thickening and
enhancement with no definite submucosal edema suggesting lymphomatous
involvement rather than inflammation.There is trace focal mesenteric stranding
and edema indicating acute inflammation.

The ascending and transverse colon are partially decompressed, but appear
normal.  Colostomy exits through the left mid abdomen, without evidence of
leak or obstruction.  The descending and sigmoid colon are surgically absent. 

Scattered calcifications and soft plaques are noted in the abdominal aorta and
iliac arteries, with patent branch vessels.  

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There are no lytic or sclerotic lesions concerning for
osseous metastatic disease.  The patient is status post posterior fusion at
L4-L5 which is unchanged in appearance.
The bones are diffusely demineralized.  There is straightening of the lumbar
lordosis.  Changes of L4-5 laminectomy and posterior fusion are present. 

IMPRESSION:

1.  Interval development of submucosal jejunal wall edema and enhancement
distal to anastomosis.  This could represent infectious or inflammatory
changes.The more distal segment demonstrates diffuse wall thickening without
edema and is concerning for lymphomatous involvement. This could be confirmed
with dedicated MR enterography.
2.  Intact ileal anastomosis and colostomy, and ___ pouch in the left
abdomen.
3.  Stable splenomegaly.
4.  Unchanged appearance of enlarged hilar and retrocardiac nodes without
additional foci of lymphadenopathy.
5.  Focal unchanged areas of scarring in the lung.
